overrides.claim: ComfyUI v0.21.1 adds and updates several image/video-generation integrations and memory/model-loading fixes; it is useful creator-stack evidence but the release is broad and mostly incremental.
FlashInfer v0.6.12 adds inference-kernel work including NVFP4 quantization, MoE kernels, GQA/MLA paths, and model/backend support relevant to low-level serving.
LongLive-2.0 applies NVFP4 across long-video training and inference, combining sequence parallelism, quantized KV cache, and streaming VAE decoding to reduce memory and increase throughput.
Frontier proposes a high-fidelity LLM inference simulator intended to model disaggregation, parallelism, runtime optimizations, and stateful agent/reasoning workloads at cluster scale.

metrics.name: simulated scale
metrics.context: Authors state the simulator scales beyond one thousand GPUs on commodity CPUs.

overrides.claim: AlignedServe proposes prefix-aware batching and orchestration to reduce intra-iteration decode bubbles in high-throughput LLM serving.

metrics.name: decode throughput improvement
metrics.context: Author-reported maximum over compared serving systems.

overrides.claim: CacheTune extends KV-cache reuse beyond strict prefixes by adaptively recomputing context needed to preserve attention relationships in long-context serving.

metrics.name: TTFT speedup
metrics.context: Author-reported TTFT speedup even with SSD/HDD cache offload.

overrides.claim: The paper argues that production LLM inference benchmarks can acquire systemic client-side measurement bias and models Python GIL effects on TTFT/TPOT using queueing analysis.
Optimus proposes elastic decoding and scheduling for diffusion language model serving to improve hardware utilization relative to fixed decoding behavior.
DisagFusion disaggregates diffusion generation stages and uses asynchronous pipeline parallelism plus elastic scheduling for heterogeneous GPU serving.

metrics.name: throughput improvement
metrics.context: Author-reported range over a monolithic baseline.

overrides.claim: The paper characterizes ReAct-style agent workloads end-to-end, tracing repeated model calls, tools, and growing context across multiple benchmarks and model configurations.
